items.remediation_detail: Cycle-17 batch-38 SCAN (2026-07-30, version_header_leakage). CONTEXT CHANGE: the pin is no longer on the 1.x line. REM-073 was applied 2026-07-24 and default.config.yml:1615 now reads uptime_kuma_version: '2.2.1' (was 1.23.13), which closed the SSTI CVE-2026-33130 (GHSA-v832-4r73-wx5j, fix 2.2.1) exactly as recommended. That major move also RETIRES the standing 'those advisories are 2.x-only, N/A to our 1.x pin' carve-out, so the whole 2.x advisory set was re-evaluated against 2.2.1 this batch: CVE-2026-32230 (ping-badge missing authz) affects 2.0.0-2.1.3, fix 2.2.0 -> COVERED; GHSA-5px6-fx2w-459r (unauth read of files beginning 'index.') affects 2.0.0-beta.0..beta.2, fix 2.0.0-beta.3 -> COVERED; GHSA-2qgm-m29m-cj2h (CVE-2024-56331 Real-Browser LFI) fix 1.23.16/2.0.0-beta.1 -> COVERED; GHSA-9fg7-wgm7-57fh (RSS CDATA stored XSS) affects <=2.0.2, fix 2.1.0 -> COVERED. NEW AND NOT COVERED: CVE-2026-45618 / GHSA-gf2q-c269-pqgc -- LiquidJS remote code execution via crafted templates (the `1|valueOf` -> `this` filter escape reaches the evaluation context), CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H against the liquidjs package itself (all versions < 10.26.0), advisory published 2026-05-27. Uptime Kuma consumes LiquidJS for NOTIFICATION TEMPLATES and shipped the dependency fix in release 2.4.0 (2026-05-31), under an explicit '### Security Fixes' heading which upstream qualifies as '(Admin only/Authenticated only)'. There is no separate louislam/uptime-kuma GHSA for it, so a version-keyed scanner querying only the uptime-kuma package will NOT flag this -- it is release-note-only, the same detection gap batch-37 recorded for freescout. The pinned 2.2.1 predates 2.4.0 and therefore carries the vulnerable liquidjs. SEVERITY MEDIUM not HIGH: the raw liquidjs CVSS is 9.8-shaped but in Uptime Kuma the template editor is an admin/authenticated surface, and the nOS posture is genuinely fail-closed at the edge -- traefik_auth_modes.uptime_kuma='proxy' with authentik@file, LIVE-CONFIRMED this batch (anonymous GET https://uptime.<tld>/ -> HTTP/2 302 to https://auth.<tld>/application/o/authorize/... with an authentik_proxy_* session cookie, i.e. the Authentik wall fires before the app sees the request), plus 127.0.0.1:3001 loopback and Tier 3. So this is insider/authenticated-admin scoped. PROBE RESULT (version_header_leakage): MOSTLY MITIGATED, one minor leak. Nothing is anonymously reachable at the edge. On the direct loopback port the service does emit 'X-Powered-By: Express' -- a stack disclosure, not a version -- and no Uptime Kuma version header. The exact version IS recoverable post-auth, but that is insider-scoped. OPERATIONAL FINDING, UNRELATED TO ANY CVE BUT MORE URGENT THAN THE CVE -- THE REM-073 REMEDIATION SILENTLY BROKE THE SERVICE. The live container has been sitting in the 2.x first-run setup wizard for six days: anonymous GET http://127.0.0.1:3001/ -> 302 to /setup-database, and the container log ends at 2026-07-24T20:49:45Z with 'db-config.json is not found or invalid: ENOENT ... Starting Setup Database ... Waiting for user action...'. The data volume (/Volumes/SSD1TB/nOS/data/platform/services/uptime_kuma/data -> /app/data) contains a ZERO-BYTE kuma.db, so the 1.23.13 monitoring database did not survive the major bump and 2.x will not self-initialise. Two consequences: (1) UPTIME MONITORING -- itself a security control, and the substrate the A9 notification fanout leans on -- has been DARK since 2026-07-24, which no gate caught because the container is 'running' and healthy; (2) the instance is parked in an UNINITIALISED SETUP WINDOW, structurally the same class as the Portainer CVE-2026-55761 finding from batch-35, differing only in that Authentik gates the route -- so it is not anonymous, but ANY authenticated Tier-3 SSO user who browses to it can complete the wizard and take the instance as admin. The presence of monitors.spec.json (26 KB, dated 2026-07-27) and setup-monitors.py in the data dir suggests a re-provisioning attempt was already started by hand and left unfinished. ALSO NOTED: roles/pazny.uptime_kuma/defaults/main.yml:16 still pins uptime_kuma_version: '1'. default.config.yml wins so 2.2.1 is what runs, and the shadow is annotated as intentional, but it is now a MAJOR-version divergence rather than a tag-convention difference and should be re-synced. The compose template's header comment ('Uptime Kuma v1.x doesn't support native OIDC ... Revisit when Uptime Kuma v2.x ships stable OIDC') is likewise stale now that 2.x is the running line. ACTION: (1) FIRST -- restore the service: complete/automate the 2.x setup-database step and re-provision monitors, then add a probe that fails when Kuma answers 302 /setup-database, so a dark monitor stack cannot pass as healthy again. (2) Bump 2.2.1 -> 2.4.0 in default.config.yml:1615 and re-sync roles/pazny.uptime_kuma/defaults/main.yml:16 off the '1' track; 2.4.0 is the current stable (2026-05-31) and is a minor move within 2.x. (3) Re-word the compose-template SSO comment.

items.remediation_detail: Cycle-18 batch-39 SCAN (2026-07-31, default_credentials_test). NEW: a five-advisory authentik wave was published 2026-07-15 and was MISSED by the last two scan-state touches -- the authentik entry carries last_checked 2026-07-16T04:06:40+02:00 but its notes are verbatim the 2026-07-06 batch-22 text, i.e. the timestamp was advanced without a re-read, and the wave landed in that gap. SOURCE NOTE (methodology, matters for future batches): these five advisories are REPO-LEVEL advisories published at api.github.com/repos/goauthentik/authentik/security-advisories and are NOT mirrored into GitHub's GLOBAL advisory database -- GET /advisories/<ghsa> returns HTTP 404 and OSV has zero records for the authentik package. A version-keyed scanner querying OSV or the global GHSA API will report authentik CLEAN and is wrong; the repo endpoint is the authoritative source for this project. EVERY advisory in the wave declares affected ranges '<= 2026.5.4' and '<= 2026.2.5', so the pinned authentik_version 2026.5.2 (default.config.yml:2232 + roles/pazny.authentik/defaults/main.yml:13, in sync) is INSIDE all of them. The wave: CVE-2026-61574 (GHSA-rv9x-92g6-9cpf, HIGH, CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H 8.8, CWE-639/863) RAC endpoint list returns every configured endpoint plus stored connection credentials to ANY authenticated user, and a connection can cross application boundaries -- exposes stored RDP/SSH/VNC credentials; CVE-2026-57580 (GHSA-35v6-hv2g-6992, HIGH, CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N 8.7, CWE-436) account takeover via SAML NameID XML-comment truncation on an inbound SAML Source; CVE-2026-54730 (GHSA-3v9h-3hrm-29cx, HIGH, CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:L/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:N 8.6, CWE-284/807) Google Chrome device-trust stage advances without confirming the out-of-band attestation ran (this one fixes at 2026.5.4/2026.2.5, one release earlier than the rest); CVE-2026-55106 (GHSA-h8ff-c3h7-2gf8, MEDIUM 5.3) LDAP Source diagnostic action omits the object-level permission filter so ANY client INCLUDING UNAUTHENTICATED ones can make the server bind to the upstream directory with the source's stored credentials and return entry DNs + attribute names; GHSA-hmrg-vpp4-gj88 (MEDIUM 5.4, CWE-862, no CVE) Shared Signals Framework checks permission only at stream CREATE, so read/update/disable/delete on an existing stream are unauthorized. APPLICABILITY TO nOS -- ALL FIVE ARE N/A AT TODAY'S CONFIGURATION, each verified rather than assumed: (1) 61574, 54730 and hmrg are ENTERPRISE-ONLY features (Remote Access Control provider, Google Chrome device-trust/Endpoint stage, Shared Signals Framework); nOS runs authentik CE with no enterprise license -- grep for enterprise|license|rac|shared signals|device.trust across roles/pazny.authentik + files/anatomy/plugins/authentik-base returns only the two MIT role-license lines. (2) 57580 requires an INBOUND SAML Source in the non-default USERNAME_LINK/EMAIL_LINK matching mode; nOS declares no SAML Source at all -- authentik is the IdP (SAML PROVIDER role, explicitly stated unaffected by the advisory), and grep for saml.*source|sources\.saml|user_matching_mode returns nothing. (3) 55106, the only UNAUTHENTICATED leg and therefore the one that would matter most, requires >=1 configured LDAP Source; nOS configures none (grep LDAPSource|sources\.ldap returns nothing) and the advisory states deployments without an LDAP Source are not affected. So this is a VERSION-DRIFT item, not a live exposure: the pin sits inside every affected range and is protected only by which authentik FEATURES nOS happens not to use, which is a configuration-conditional defence that silently expires the day an operator adds an LDAP or SAML Source (the LDAP leg would then be anonymously reachable, since auth.<tld> is public by design -- traefik_auth_modes.authentik='none', authentik IS the auth provider). ACTION: bump authentik_version 2026.5.2 -> 2026.5.6 in default.config.yml:2232 AND roles/pazny.authentik/defaults/main.yml:13 together. 2026.5.6 (2026-07-22) is the latest release and is >= the 2026.5.5 fix floor; the intermediate 2026.5.3 (bugfix) and 2026.5.4 ride along. Same-minor move, no blueprint or schema change expected. REM-013/021/060 remain resolved; the 2026.5.1 SAML/Source cluster (CVE-2026-49448 CRIT 9.8 SourceStage empty-POST bypass, CVE-2026-42849 CRIT 9.3 SFE reflected XSS, CVE-2026-47201 HIGH 8.5 XML signature wrapping, CVE-2026-49443 HIGH 8.8) stays covered at 2026.5.2 and is unaffected by this item.

items.remediation_detail: Cycle-18 batch-39 SCAN (2026-07-31, default_credentials_test). Surfaced while scanning the grafana component and initially dismissed as 'a separate product nOS does not deploy' -- that dismissal was WRONG and is corrected here: `docker ps` shows iiab-mcp-grafana-1 running mcp/grafana:latest, rendered by roles/pazny.mcp_gateway/templates/compose.yml.j2:66-81 and wired into mcpo via roles/pazny.mcp_gateway/templates/mcpo-config.json.j2:23 ('grafana' -> http://mcp-grafana:8000/sse). The prior grafana scan-state note asserting no image-renderer / no separate Grafana component was reasoning about the WRONG sidecar. CVE-2026-15583 (Grafana security advisory, published 2026-07-15, HIGH, CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:N/A:N 8.6): a confused-deputy SSRF in the mcp-grafana project -- the attacker-supplied X-Grafana-URL request header overrides the server's configured Grafana base URL, so mcp-grafana issues its outbound call, CARRYING ITS ENVIRONMENT-CONFIGURED SERVICE-ACCOUNT TOKEN, to an attacker-chosen destination. PR:N -- exploitation requires NO authentication to mcp-grafana itself. Fixed in mcp-grafana 0.17.1. THE PIN IS THE PROBLEM AND IT IS A FLOATING-TAG STALENESS BUG, not merely an unpinned version: mcp_grafana_version defaults to 'latest', and the locally-pulled image was BUILT 2026-07-08 (docker image inspect .Created) -- seven days BEFORE the 2026-07-15 fix -- and has not been re-pulled since, so the running container is on pre-0.17.1 code. The binary self-reports '(devel)' with no semver, so neither a human nor a version-keyed scanner can confirm the version from the image; the build date is the only evidence, and it points the wrong way. WHAT LEAKS: compose.yml.j2:71 sets GRAFANA_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN, populated with a real token by roles/pazny.mcp_gateway/tasks/post.yml:108 -- that token is exactly what the advisory describes exfiltrating, and it is a live Grafana service-account credential, so its disclosure is a direct pivot into Grafana. REACHABILITY -- MITIGATED, stated honestly and NOT rated as internet-anonymous: `docker port iiab-mcp-grafana-1` returns 8000/tcp -> null, i.e. the container publishes NO host port; it is absent from state/manifest.yml so services.yml.j2 derives NO Traefik router for it; it is reachable only on iiab_net and the flat {{ stacks_shared_network }}. The fronting mcpo IS routed but is defended twice over -- traefik_auth_modes.mcp_gateway='proxy' (authentik@file forward-auth) and mcpo's own --api-key -- and mcpo opens its own SSE session from its static config rather than proxying client headers, so edge-to-SSRF header injection through mcpo is NOT established (I did not verify mcpo's header handling by test; treat that leg as unverified rather than as ruled out). Net: the realistic exploit path is a foothold in ANY other container on iiab_net or shared_net -- a broad blast radius given SEC-02 already documents shared_net as flat -- making this container-adjacent lateral movement plus credential theft, not anonymous remote compromise. That is why it is filed HIGH rather than CRITICAL despite the 8.6/PR:N base score. ACTION: pin mcp_grafana_version to an explicit >= 0.17.1 tag in roles/pazny.mcp_gateway/defaults/main.yml instead of 'latest' (a floating tag is what let a 3-week-old vulnerable image sit resident), then re-pull and recreate: `docker compose -p iiab pull mcp-grafana && docker compose -p iiab up -d mcp-grafana`. Because the token is assumed reachable for as long as the vulnerable image ran, ROTATE the Grafana service account token afterwards -- tasks/post.yml already re-provisions it, so a --tags mcp_gateway run after the bump closes both legs. STRUCTURAL FOLLOW-UP: mcp_grafana_version:'latest' is the same unpinned-floating-tag class as the nextcloud ':33' note in this batch; both defeat version-keyed CVE scanning by design.

items.fix_version: config change (extend the weak-prefix assert to local tenants, or generate a random prefix on first run)
items.remediation_detail: Cycle-18 batch-39 PROBE OF RECORD (2026-07-31, default_credentials_test). This is the designated probe's finding and it is a genuine shipped-default-credential exposure, reached by reading the config chain rather than by guessing. THE CHAIN, each link verified: (1) default.config.yml:8 ships the literal `global_password_prefix: "changeme"` -- a committed, world-readable value in a public repo. (2) The operator override lives in credentials.yml, which `git check-ignore -v` confirms is ignored at .gitignore:12 and `git ls-files` confirms is NOT tracked -- so a FRESH CLONE HAS NO credentials.yml AND THE EFFECTIVE PREFIX IS 'changeme'. (3) The guard that exists, main.yml:1257 '[Security] Refuse a weak password prefix on a public tenant' (asserts prefix not in ['changeme',''] and length >= 12), is gated `when: not (tenant_domain_is_local | default(true) | bool)`. default.config.yml:131 derives tenant_domain_is_local by testing whether tenant_domain ends in .local/.lan/.test/.localhost, and the default tenant_domain IS dev.local -- so on the DEFAULT install the flag is TRUE and THE ASSERT IS SKIPPED. The guard's own comment says so out loud ('lenient for local dev.local'), so this is a deliberate carve-out whose blast radius was under-estimated, not an oversight. (4) The prefix prompt at main.yml:1058 fires ONLY on a confirmed removal (remove=data|deep|all + confirm=true); a plain first `ansible-playbook main.yml` NEVER prompts, and even on a removal run bare ENTER re-accepts the current value. So the default path is silent: no prompt, no assert, no warning. WHAT 'changeme' THEN UNLOCKS, for the components in this batch's scope -- every one of these is a deterministic, publicly-computable string, not a guess: authentik akadmin / changeme_pw_authentik_admin (default.credentials.yml:315 authentik_bootstrap_password), which is the IdP SUPERUSER and therefore the entire SSO fabric, every downstream native_oidc/header_oidc/forward_auth service at once; grafana admin / changeme_pw_grafana (default.config.yml:1377-1378); nextcloud admin / changeme_pw_nextcloud_admin (default.config.yml:1254-1255); plus authentik_db_password changeme_pw_authentik_db and mcpo_api_key changeme_pw_mcpo (roles/pazny.mcp_gateway/defaults/main.yml:22). The username halves are themselves the shipped literals 'admin' / 'akadmin'. REACHABILITY: services bind 127.0.0.1 by default (services_lan_access=false), but Traefik binds 0.0.0.0:443 and routes all three -- traefik_auth_modes grafana='oidc' and nextcloud='oidc' mean the router answers 200 anonymously and the service's OWN login form is served (native OIDC adds a 'Sign in with Authentik' button, it does NOT remove local password auth), and authentik='none' because it is the auth provider. So from LAN/Tailscale, a client with the right Host header reaches a live local-credential login form for each. Note the second-order effect: a local admin login BYPASSES the Authentik MFA posture entirely, since MFA is enforced in the Authentik flow the local form never enters. VERIFIED NOT AFFECTED, and worth recording because it is the highest-value key and it is handled CORRECTLY: authentik_secret_key is declared prefix-derived at default.credentials.yml:313 but main.yml:1299 lazy-regenerates any value containing '_pw_' or shorter than 50 chars into `openssl rand -hex 50` and persists it to ~/.nos/secrets.yml. The Django SECRET_KEY that signs authentik session cookies is therefore NOT derivable from the prefix, and the cookie-forgery path that would have made this trivially CRITICAL does not exist. The same regeneration group covers outline/infisical/bluesky/paperclip/hedgedoc/bone secrets, and as of REM-144 face_edge_token. THIS HOST IS NOT EXPLOITABLE: the operator's untracked credentials.yml:11 sets a non-default 13-char prefix, so the live tenant does not carry 'changeme'. The finding is about what a FRESH install of this playbook provisions by default, which is precisely the default_credentials_test probe's remit. Rated HIGH rather than CRITICAL because it requires operator inaction rather than being unconditionally live; the IMPACT if triggered is full-tenant compromise. RELATIONSHIP TO REM-144: complementary, not duplicate. REM-144 (resolved 2026-07-30) was about the prefix being DISCLOSED through the Traefik API and carries the operator residual 'if 443 was reachable from outside this host, the exposed password prefix must be treated as disclosed'. REM-151 is about the prefix being GUESSABLE BY DEFAULT in the first place. Both converge on the same weakness that every admin credential is a pure function of one shared string with no per-service entropy. ACTION, in order of preference: (a) generate a random prefix on first run when none is supplied (mirrors the main.yml:1299 lazy-regenerate pattern already proven for secret_key) -- removes the failure mode instead of warning about it; (b) at minimum, drop the `not tenant_domain_is_local` condition from main.yml:1257 so the assert also fires on dev.local, keeping the documented `-e allow_weak_prefix=true` bypass for throwaway dev boxes; (c) give the admin-password class its own random-per-service generation rather than prefix derivation. Add a pytest gate under tests/anatomy/ pinning that 'changeme' cannot survive a default-tenant run, so this cannot regress silently.
items.resolved_by: Already fixed on 2026-08-02 by 4e958788 ("feat(security): P0 + P4 — measure the blast radius, drop the carve-out"), two days after this row was raised, and the queue never learned. The `tenant_domain_is_local` carve-out is gone from the weak-prefix assert (main.yml); its only remaining condition is the explicit `-e allow_weak_prefix=true` operator bypass, and it carries tags: [always] so a tag-filtered run cannot skip it. The shipped `changeme` default therefore fails the run closed on EVERY tenant rather than being silently used by a fresh clone, which was this finding's actual exposure. The default is deliberately left as the sentinel: an obvious value that refuses is safer than a generated one that works. Nothing pinned the removal until 2026-08-06 — gate tests/anatomy/test_the_weak_prefix_gate_has_no_carve_out.py, which finds the assert by what it asserts rather than by its name (the task was renamed when the carve-out went, so a name-keyed gate would go red on a rename and blind on the condition).

items.remediation_detail: Cycle-19 batch-40 SCAN (2026-08-01, ssrf_vector_analysis). OVERTURNS the 2026-07-18 batch-29 disposition 'NOW CLEAN ... NO n8n advisory published after the June-24 cluster in the window'. That was WRONG WHEN WRITTEN: the 2026-07-08 wave was already ten days old at the time. TWO waves are now missed and the pinned n8n_version 2.28.1 (default.config.yml:1475 + roles/pazny.n8n/defaults/main.yml:10, in sync; live-confirmed n8nio/n8n:2.28.1 running as iiab-n8n-1) sits below BOTH fix floors. METHODOLOGY -- the reason this was missed, same defect class as the authentik entry in batch-39: n8n publishes REPO-LEVEL advisories with NO CVE IDs assigned (all 25 below have cve_id: null). batch-29 queried community.n8n.io bulletins / OpenCVE / CCCS -- all CVE-keyed -- and correctly found nothing, because there is nothing CVE-keyed to find. Query api.github.com/repos/n8n-io/n8n/security-advisories or miss the entire product. OSV DOES carry them (npm ecosystem): a version-aware OSV query for n8n@2.28.1 returns 29 vulns. WAVE A (2026-07-08, 11 advisories, fixed 2.29.8 / 2.30.1): GHSA-pm35-fqvh-cq5g (HIGH 8.9, legacy expression evaluator sanitizer bypass -> authenticated code execution), GHSA-9wcp-9r3j-383q (HIGH 8.4, stored DOM XSS via resource-locator cachedResultUrl), GHSA-35q8-9mj6-wjmf (HIGH 7.7, SSO instance-role provisioning -> privilege escalation to instance owner -- DIRECTLY relevant, nOS wires n8n to Authentik native OIDC), GHSA-x5vx-c2c8-m3w9 (HIGH 7.2, AI-Agents project-viewer priv-esc via run_node_tool), GHSA-777w-rpr6-c52h (HIGH, full public-API-key scope assignment to token-exchange JWTs), GHSA-9w78-79q7-r4fp (MED 6.3, authenticated SSRF via dynamic node-parameters endpoints -> internal network access), GHSA-q5xf-xhwf-cwqf (MED 5.1), GHSA-89gh-3pgc-v5h2 (MED 5.1, custom-header credential values leaked in plaintext into LLM node execution data), GHSA-fpg6-x68q-5793 (MED 5.5), GHSA-33q9-f52j-gc75 (MED 6.3 -- the ONE item 2.28.1 already covers, fixed 2.27.4/2.28.0). WAVE B (2026-07-22, 15 advisories, fixed 2.31.5 / 2.32.1): GHSA-8342-988q-86cr (HIGH 8.9, account takeover via unverified email claim in token-exchange embed login), GHSA-gv7g-jm28-cr3m (HIGH 8.7, expression sandbox escape via arrow-function bodies -> command execution), GHSA-rcv6-pvrj-4xcg (HIGH 8.7, authenticated code execution in the Git node), GHSA-2x35-3fw4-9jr4 (HIGH 8.2, Send Email node arbitrary file read AND SSRF via nodemailer content-object type confusion), GHSA-xmc9-4f2h-jf9c (HIGH 7.7, Edit Image node format injection -> arbitrary file write), GHSA-cj9h-qx8g-pq2g (HIGH 7.2, shared-workflow editor exfiltrates credentials via inline sub-workflow JSON), GHSA-64xh-79j6-r5v8 (HIGH 7.1, bypass of the 'Allowed HTTP Request Domains' credential restriction in multiple AI/LLM nodes), GHSA-6qc9-mqvw-jg7x (HIGH 7.1, credential authorization bypass via expression in HTTP Request node genericAuthType), GHSA-gf29-4f56-r2jf (HIGH 7.1, Git node fetch/pull/pushTags bypass sandbox path restriction), GHSA-xwx6-jjhv-84p8 (HIGH 7.1, prototype pollution via dot-notation field names -> instance-wide DoS), GHSA-vhf8-cg2h-cg3p (MED 6.4, SSRF protection bypass via MCP Client node), GHSA-hx4h-vr3m-45vh (MED 6.1), GHSA-9cmh-xcqm-5hqr (MED 5.8, cross-tenant module-cache poisoning in the JS task runner), GHSA-652q-gvq3-74qv (MED 5.3, Snowflake node SQL injection), GHSA-pf2q-pxhf-hgmw (MED 4.9). SEVERITY RATIONALE -- filed HIGH, deliberately NOT CRITICAL: the ceiling across all 25 is 8.9 (CVSS 4.0) and GitHub labels every one of them High or Moderate. None is a CRITICAL and none is unauthenticated-RCE, so inflating the aggregate to CRITICAL would misrepresent the sources. What makes it urgent is breadth (four independent sandbox-escape / code-execution paths, two 8.9 account-takeover-class items) and the SSRF cluster below, not any single score. PROBE (ssrf_vector_analysis) -- THE FINDING OF RECORD FOR THIS BATCH. Four of the 25 are SSRF-class, and they land on precisely the control REM-043 installed. GHSA-vhf8-cg2h-cg3p is the direct hit: 'The MCP Client node sends requests to user-supplied endpoints WITHOUT routing them through SSRF protection and WITHOUT PINNING THE RESOLVED ADDRESS' (advisory text, verified on the GitHub advisory page), CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:L/UI:N/VC:L/VI:N/VA:N/SC:H/SI:H/SA:L = 6.4. PR:L -- 'an authenticated user who could create or edit a workflow', i.e. the DEFAULT workflow:create permission. So N8N_SSRF_PROTECTION_ENABLED='true' -- which the n8n-base plugin compose-extension sets and which closed REM-043 -- is simply NOT CONSULTED on that node's egress. GHSA-64xh-79j6-r5v8 (HIGH 7.1) independently bypasses the 'Allowed HTTP Request Domains' credential allow-list across the AI/LLM nodes; GHSA-9w78-79q7-r4fp reaches the internal network through the dynamic node-parameters endpoints; GHSA-2x35-3fw4-9jr4 adds SSRF plus arbitrary file read through nodemailer type confusion. IMPACT IS THE FULL REM-043 IMPACT, RESTORED: the n8n container sits on iiab_net AND the flat {{stacks_shared_network}}, so an SSRF primitive reaches postgresql, redis, mariadb, prometheus, portainer and every peer service by container name. SEC-02 does NOT cover this -- SEC-02 moved the header-trust backends onto gated nets; n8n is not one of them and still holds shared_net. Rated EXPLOITABLE, not theoretical, with the honest precondition that it is AUTHENTICATED: n8n is traefik_auth_modes.n8n='oidc' (native, 200 at edge, own login) and registration is SSO-provisioned, so the attacker population is 'any tenant user with a workflow seat', not the internet. Host port is 127.0.0.1:5678 loopback (services_lan_access=false). DO NOT REOPEN REM-043 -- its control is correct and still blocks the HTTP Request node; what changed is that upstream shipped nodes that route around it. The durable lesson: an in-app SSRF allow-list is a per-node property and regresses silently with every new node, so it cannot be the only layer. ACTION: bump n8n_version 2.28.1 -> 2.32.7 in default.config.yml:1475 AND roles/pazny.n8n/defaults/main.yml:10 TOGETHER (version-pin shadow: default.config.yml wins). 2.32.7 published 2026-07-31 and IS the current 'stable' release tag; it is >= the 2.32.1 fix floor and clears BOTH waves. Minimum safe is 2.32.1. Latest overall is 2.33.3 (2026-07-31) but that is the fast-moving line -- prefer stable. Same-major (2.x) migrate-on-start, so no coexistence track; validate workflows on the next converge. INTERIM MITIGATION if the bump must wait: set NODES_EXCLUDE for the MCP Client node (upstream's own documented workaround) and/or network-level egress restriction -- note this is exactly what n8n recommends because the in-app guard is the thing that failed.

Cycle-19 batch-40 SCAN (2026-08-01, ssrf_vector_analysis). OVERTURNS the 2026-07-18 batch-29 disposition 'CLEAN/re-verified at pinned metabase_version v0.61.2.6 ... NO new Metabase OSS CVE past the pin in the window' -- by six days. GHSA-cwxq-fmxq-jv8h was published 2026-07-12T08:38:51Z, before that scan ran. METHODOLOGY -- the same repo-level blind spot as n8n/REM-152 and authentik/REM-149, and the reason batch-29's sentence is literally true yet wrong: this advisory has NO CVE ID (cve_id: null). A scan phrased as 'no new Metabase OSS *CVE*' cannot see it. Metabase publishes to api.github.com/repos/metabase/metabase/security-advisories, where 15 advisories are listed and SIX of the last ten carry no CVE at all. VERSION MAPPING, stated explicitly because it is what makes the range apply: Metabase numbers OSS as v0.X.Y and the corresponding Enterprise build as v1.X.Y from the same source tree, and the advisories are written against the 1.x numbers. The pin v0.61.2.6 therefore reads as 1.61.2.6 for range comparison. THE FINDING: GHSA-cwxq-fmxq-jv8h, CRITICAL, 'Arbitrary File Read/Write via Unsafe H2 Built-in Functions'. Metabase did not restrict the H2 built-ins FILE_READ, FILE_WRITE, CSVREAD, CSVWRITE and LINK_SCHEMA, so a user who can run a native query or action against an H2 data source can read arbitrary files off the Metabase container, write files to it, and open connections to other databases. Affected ranges: >=1.55.0 <1.58.16, >=1.59.0 <1.59.13, >=1.60.0 <1.60.9, >=1.61.0 <1.61.4. The pin 1.61.2.6 falls inside >=1.61.0 <1.61.4 = AFFECTED. Patched 1.58.16 / 1.59.13 / 1.60.9 / 1.61.4 'and matching 0.x releases' -- upstream states the 0.x OSS line is patched too, so this is NOT one of the Enterprise-only H2 items. That distinction matters here: CVE-2026-33725 (the H2 JDBC INIT injection dismissed as N/A in batch-29) genuinely WAS EE-only; this one is not, and the earlier correct dismissal should not be read across to it. EXPOSED BY DEFAULT, which is what carries the CRITICAL: upstream notes the bundled SAMPLE DATABASE IS H2, so no operator has to attach an H2 source for the primitive to exist -- it ships attached. Any principal with query permission has it. PRECONDITION AND WHO HOLDS IT, stated honestly: this is AUTHENTICATED, not anonymous. But the nOS-specific aggravation is that Metabase OSS has no OIDC, so per docs/sso-and-attribution.md it runs as a Traefik forward_auth gate (traefik_auth_modes.metabase='proxy') in front of a SHARED Metabase account. Every tenant user who clears the Authentik wall therefore lands on the SAME query-capable identity -- there is no per-user Metabase authorization to fall back on, and no per-user attribution in the audit trail either. PROBE (ssrf_vector_analysis): LINK_SCHEMA is the SSRF-relevant leg and is why this surfaced under this probe rather than a pure CVE sweep -- it 'establishes connections to other databases' from inside the container, i.e. an attacker-directed outbound connection primitive with no allow-list, which is an SSRF by any definition even though the advisory does not use the word. The container is on data_net AND the flat {{stacks_shared_network}} (roles/pazny.metabase/templates/compose.yml.j2), so that primitive reaches postgresql, redis, mariadb and every peer by container name -- and FILE_READ additionally discloses the container's own MB_DB_PASS from the environment. This is the SECOND component this batch whose SSRF exposure is an amplifier of flat-shared_net membership; see REM-152. Rated EXPLOITABLE. Live-confirmed: metabase/metabase:v0.61.2.6 running as data-metabase-1, host port 127.0.0.1:3002 loopback. ACTION: bump metabase_version v0.61.2.6 -> v0.61.9 in default.config.yml:2066 AND roles/pazny.metabase/defaults/main.yml:10 TOGETHER (version-pin shadow: default.config.yml wins). v0.61.9 was published 2026-07-28 and is >= the 0.61.4 fix floor while STAYING ON THE 0.61 LINE -- a patch move, no Flyway major migration. Do NOT jump to v0.62.7 (latest) in the same step: that is a minor-line move on a service whose first-boot migration already needs a 300s start_period. Verify the running image tag after the converge -- this component has a documented version-pin shadow history. PRIOR ITEMS RE-CHECKED AND STILL COVERED AT THE PIN (each range checked, not assumed): CVE-2026-59827 (GHSA-w95f-x9v9-wv36, CRIT 9.9, unsafe deserialization of H2 query results) fixes at 1.61.1.4 and 1.61.2.6 > 1.61.1.4 = NOT affected; CVE-2026-59826 (GHSA-8wx2-rxp2-4x35, CRIT 9.1) fixes at 1.61.2 = NOT affected; CVE-2026-50148 (GHSA-r6x2-rchx-q9g9, CRIT 10.0, Snowflake JDBC RCE) and CVE-2026-50147 (GHSA-mfpj-crjq-xrcp, HIGH 7.6) declare no 1.61 range at all, topping out at 1.60.x = NOT affected; the 2026-05-27 five-item MEDIUM cluster (incl. GHSA-rxq7-9vqf-q9g8, the only UNAUTHENTICATED one -- entity-ID to internal-ID translation endpoints) also tops out at 1.60.x = NOT affected. REM-026/053/056 remain resolved. PIN APPLIED 2026-08-01 (default.config.yml:2066 + roles/pazny.metabase/defaults/main.yml:10, both halves per the version-pin-shadow rule). NOT yet live-verified: the running container is still v0.61.2.6 until the next converge recreates it — re-derive from `docker ps`, do not inherit this line.

Cycle-19 batch-40 ssrf_vector_analysis finding (NOT a CVE -- this is a configuration property and survives the 2.93 upgrade that just resolved REM-106; the parser CVEs and this are independent). THE CONFIG: the Ansible-managed block in tasks/dnsmasq.yml emits address=, listen-address=, bind-interfaces, local=/<tenant_domain>/ and cache-size=1000. It does NOT emit `stop-dns-rebind`, and dnsmasq's rebind filter is OFF by default. Because `local=` scopes authority to the tenant domain only, every OTHER name is forwarded upstream and the upstream answer is returned verbatim -- including answers that point into 127.0.0.0/8 or RFC-1918. That is textbook DNS rebinding relay. LIVE-CONFIRMED, not inferred: `dig +short @127.0.0.1 localtest.me A` returned 127.0.0.1 on this host. localtest.me is a public name whose authoritative answer IS 127.0.0.1, so it is a safe, non-destructive stand-in for an attacker-controlled rebinding domain -- with stop-dns-rebind set, dnsmasq would have filtered that answer and returned nothing. The control query `dig +short @1.1.1.1 localtest.me A` returned the same 127.0.0.1, confirming the answer is genuinely upstream's and the resolver is relaying rather than synthesising it. Effective config re-read from {{homebrew_prefix}}/etc/dnsmasq.conf confirms no stop-dns-rebind / rebind-domain-ok / rebind-localhost-ok directive is present anywhere (the only rebind-adjacent lines in the file are upstream's commented-out samples). REACHABILITY -- and this is where the finding must be scoped honestly, because the obvious over-claim is wrong. dnsmasq binds 127.0.0.1 AND the en0 LAN address (listen-address=127.0.0.1,<lan-ip> + bind-interfaces), because dnsmasq_lan_access defaults TRUE. So it is a general-purpose forwarding resolver for any LAN or Tailscale client configured to use this host -- which is the documented purpose of that flag ('for TVs, mobiles, guests'). For THAT population the rebinding relay is real and unauthenticated. WHAT IT IS NOT: this does NOT chain into the container-side SSRF findings of this same batch (REM-152 n8n, REM-153 metabase), and it would be wrong to score it as if it did. Docker containers resolve via Docker's embedded DNS (127.0.0.11) which forwards to the Docker Desktop VM's upstream, not to host dnsmasq; and on the host side /etc/resolver/<tenant_domain> is a DOMAIN-SCOPED macOS resolver entry, so mDNSResponder consults dnsmasq only for the tenant domain and uses the normal system upstream for everything else. dnsmasq is therefore NOT in the resolution path for the attacker-controlled external names that a rebinding attack against n8n or metabase would need. Rated EXPLOITABLE for LAN-resolver clients, THEORETICAL as an SSRF amplifier for the container fleet. It is filed because it is the substrate that would silently become load-bearing the day containers or the host are pointed at dnsmasq as a general resolver -- a one-line change away. IMPACT for the in-scope population: a LAN client browsing an attacker page gets a short-TTL name that flips to 127.0.0.1 or 192.168.x, and the browser's same-origin policy then treats attacker JS as same-origin with services on that client's own loopback/LAN -- including, on the operator's own workstation, the loopback-bound nOS admin surfaces (portainer 9002, metabase 3002, n8n 5678, alloy 12345) that every other finding in this queue correctly treats as protected BY that loopback bind. ACTION: add `stop-dns-rebind` to the managed block in tasks/dnsmasq.yml. Add `rebind-localhost-ok` alongside it -- REQUIRED, not optional, because the tenant domain is itself answered as 127.0.0.1 on a local-TLD install (dnsmasq_dev_address) and a bare stop-dns-rebind would filter nOS's own *.dev.local answers and break the entire platform by name. If any legitimate upstream domain must resolve to a private address, exempt it with `rebind-domain-ok=/<domain>/` rather than dropping the guard. Consider also documenting dnsmasq_lan_access=false for operators who do not need the guest-device use case, which removes the exposed population entirely. Gate the rendered directive with a tests/anatomy/ assertion so it cannot regress. items.remediation_detail: Cycle-21 batch-42 ATTACK PROBE (tls_crypto_weakness) -- LIVE-CONFIRMED, and it is a config-says-one-thing-runtime-does-another defect, not a cipher weakness. roles/pazny.traefik/templates/traefik.yml.j2 sets entryPoints.websecure.http.tls.options = 'modern@file', and dynamic/middlewares.yml.j2 defines tls.options.modern with minVersion VersionTLS13. The intent is a TLS-1.3-only edge. The runtime disagrees: GET http://127.0.0.1:8082/api/http/routers shows EVERY file-provider router resolving tls = {"options": "default"} -- wordpress@file, hedgedoc@file, bookstack@file, gitlab@file all identical. Cause: dynamic/services.yml.j2 emits a bare `tls: {}` on each router (lines ~60 and ~105); a router that declares its own tls block does not inherit the entry point's http.tls.options, and Traefik normalizes the empty block to the 'default' option set. So the EFFECTIVE policy is tls.options.default = minVersion VersionTLS12 + the seven-entry AEAD cipher list, and 'modern' is attached to nothing. Live probe against 127.0.0.1:443: TLS 1.3 negotiates TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 (Verification OK, X25519, SHA256); a forced -tls1_2 handshake SUCCEEDS at ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256 -- which is entry five of the `default` cipherSuites list, proving that block is the one in force; -tls1_1 is refused (no protocols available); and a TLS-1.2 handshake restricted to CBC suites (ECDHE-RSA-AES256-SHA384:ECDHE-RSA-AES128-SHA) is refused with alert 40, proving the AEAD-only restriction holds. VERDICT: MITIGATED as a crypto posture -- TLS 1.2 with ECDHE + AEAD-only and no CBC/RC4/3DES/export suites is not a weakness, and TLS <=1.1 is dead. The finding is that the operator's declared 'modern' profile has never been in effect, so a future hardening edit to the modern block would silently do nothing. ACTION (pick one): (a) drop the per-router `tls: {}` in services.yml.j2 so routers inherit the entry point's modern@file, or (b) emit `tls: {options: modern@file}` per router, or (c) if TLS 1.2 support is deliberate for older clients, DELETE the modern block and the entry-point option line so the config states the truth. Recommend (b) -- explicit, survives the anti-loop/extra-router branches, and keeps a single grep-able source. Add a pytest gate asserting no rendered router carries a bare empty tls block.

items.remediation_detail: Cycle-21 batch-42 ATTACK PROBE (tls_crypto_weakness). WordPress is the ONLY one of the five scanned services with no HTTPS-awareness behind the TLS-terminating edge. Traefik terminates TLS and reaches the container over cleartext -- GET /api/http/services shows wordpress@file -> http://wordpress:80 -- and grep across the whole role finds NO WORDPRESS_CONFIG_EXTRA, no FORCE_SSL_ADMIN, no $_SERVER['HTTPS'] derivation from HTTP_X_FORWARDED_PROTO, in the compose template, tasks, or any of the five mu-plugins. PHP therefore sees $_SERVER['HTTPS'] unset and SERVER_PORT 80, so WordPress core is_ssl() returns FALSE. Consequence: wp_set_auth_cookie() defaults its $secure argument to is_ssl(), and wp-login.php only forces $secure_cookie when force_ssl_admin() is on or the user carries the per-user use_ssl option -- neither applies here -- so the POST-LOGIN authentication cookie is issued WITHOUT the Secure attribute. Partially self-masking on inspection: the login page's wordpress_test_cookie IS emitted `secure; HttpOnly` (live-verified) because that one derives from the wp_login_url() scheme, which is https since `wp core install --url=https://...` (roles/pazny.wordpress/tasks/post.yml:59) stored siteurl/home as https -- so a header glance suggests the cookies are fine when the auth cookie is the one that is not. Exploit path: :80 is live and answers the request before redirecting (live-verified `HTTP/1.1 301 Moved Permanently` for http://wordpress.<tld>/wp-admin/), so a non-Secure cookie is transmitted in cleartext on any plaintext navigation to the host, recoverable by an on-path observer. STRONG MITIGATION, which is why this is MEDIUM and not HIGH: security-headers@file sets strict-transport-security max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains on every response (live-verified on all four running services), so any browser that has seen one nOS response upgrades the request before it leaves -- residual is first-contact / HSTS-unseeded clients and non-browser agents. Contrast with the peers, all correct: hedgedoc sets CMD_PROTOCOL_USESSL=true and emits connect.sid HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; bookstack's APP_URL=https drives Laravel session.php `'secure' => env('SESSION_SECURE_COOKIE', null) ?? Str::startsWith(env('APP_URL',''),'https:')` and emits bookstack_session secure; httponly; samesite=lax; gitlab's external_url https drives _gitlab_session secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=None. ACTION: add WORDPRESS_CONFIG_EXTRA to roles/pazny.wordpress/templates/compose.yml.j2 setting $_SERVER['HTTPS']='on' when HTTP_X_FORWARDED_PROTO is https, plus define('FORCE_SSL_ADMIN', true); this is the documented docker-official-image pattern and fixes is_ssl() for every downstream consumer, not just cookies. Trust the header only because the container is reachable solely via the edge (127.0.0.1:8084 loopback publish, no LAN bind).

items.remediation_detail: Cycle-21 batch-42 ATTACK PROBE (tls_crypto_weakness). tasks/tls-certs.yml, task '[mkcert] Ensure cert files are world-readable (Traefik container UID reads them)', chmods BOTH ssl_cert_path and ssl_cert_key to 0644 -- i.e. the PRIVATE KEY of the local wildcard certificate is world-readable. That key signs *.<tenant_domain>, *.<apps_subdomain>.<tenant_domain>, localhost/127.0.0.1/::1 and (when bluesky is on) *.dev.lan, and the matching mkcert root CA is installed into the system trust store by `mkcert -install`, so any local process running as any user can read it and impersonate every nOS service to any browser on the machine with a certificate the OS trusts. The stated justification does not hold: traefik_certs_dir is bind-mounted read-only into the container (live: /Users/pazny/stacks/infra/tls:/certs:ro) and the traefik container declares no User, so it runs as root inside its namespace and reads an operator-owned 0600 file through the bind mount without trouble. NOT LIVE ON THIS HOST: the operator runs the public-TLD path (tenant_domain=pazny.eu, so tenant_domain_is_local is false and the mkcert block is skipped); the ACME material that IS present is correctly locked down -- ~/stacks/infra/tls/acme is drwx------. So this is a latent defect on the local-TLD path that every .local/.lan/.test install and every CI/dev blank takes. Blast radius on a single-operator Mac is limited by there being one human user, but it is not limited to humans: any container that bind-mounts a parent of that path, and any unprivileged agent process on the host, inherits read on the key. ACTION: set mode 0600 on ssl_cert_key (leave the certificate at 0644 -- a public cert is public) and delete the misleading task name/comment; if a future non-root container image genuinely needs read, use 0640 plus a group the container UID is in, never world-read. Add a pytest gate asserting no task in tasks/tls-certs.yml applies a world-readable mode to a *_key path.

Cycle-22 batch-43 CVE scan (2026-08-05, resource_exhaustion_vectors). OVERTURNS TWO consecutive 'CLEAN/re-verified at version-6.2.21' dispositions (batch-23 2026-07-08 and batch-31 2026-07-21) -- and this is a COVERAGE gap, not a fresh disclosure. Both prior scans enumerated exactly two in-window advisories and correctly showed both MISSING the pin: GHSA-5q8v-j673-m5v4 (User-API IDOR, affects >=6.4.23, so 6.2.21 predates the vulnerable code) and GHSA-29w6-c52g-m8jc (CSV injection, affects <6.1.7, so 6.2.21 postdates the fix). There is a THIRD, and it was published BEFORE BOTH of those scans: GHSA-6jq6-x4cx-qvcm, 'Firefly III has Stored XSS in Audit Log Entry view via piggy bank name (ale.twig)', repo-published 2026-05-21, global-DB-published 2026-06-12. It is MODERATE, CVSS 4.0 AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:L/UI:P/VC:L/VI:L/VA:N/SC:L/SI:L/SA:N, no CVE assigned. THE RANGE IS THE POINT: OSV declares the affected interval as introduced 0 -> fixed 6.6.3 -- i.e. EVERY version ever released below 6.6.3, so the pin is not merely inside the window, it can never have been outside it. A version-aware OSV query for Packagist grumpydictator/firefly-iii at 6.2.21 returns this advisory as a direct hit; the same query against the package name firefly-iii/firefly-iii returns zero, which is the likely mechanism of the original miss (Firefly's Packagist name is grumpydictator/firefly-iii, not the GitHub org/repo path). MECHANISM: resources/views/list/ale.twig renders the piggy-bank name from AuditLogEntry.after.piggy through Twig's |raw filter. The |raw is needed on the outer trans() call to preserve the <span> currency-styling tags in the amount parameter, but it also disables auto-escaping for the user-controlled name parameter -- so a piggy bank created with an HTML payload in its name executes arbitrary JavaScript in any browser that later views that transaction's audit log. SCOPE, stated honestly: PR:L + UI:P means an authenticated user must plant the payload and a second user must view the affected audit log; in a single-operator install the attacker and the victim are the same person, which is why this is MEDIUM and not HIGH. It becomes real on a multi-tenant or shared-household Firefly. ACTION: bump firefly_version version-6.2.21 -> version-6.6.3 or later in roles/pazny.firefly/defaults/main.yml:15 (grep-confirmed NO default.config.yml shadow -- the role default is authoritative for this service, unlike erpnext/homeassistant). This also retires the standing 'HYGIENE: 6.2.21 trails current 6.5.x' note that both prior scans carried without an item, and lands past GHSA-5q8v's >=6.4.23 introduction, so verify GHSA-5q8v-j673-m5v4 (User-API IDOR) is fixed at the chosen target -- its fix is 6.5.4, so any target >=6.6.3 clears it. Cycle-22 batch-43 CVE scan + ATTACK PROBE (2026-08-05, resource_exhaustion_vectors). SUCCESSOR to REM-132 (resolved -- the pin advanced v2.23.0 -> v2.26.3, live-verified iiab-ntfy-1 on binwiederhier/ntfy:v2.26.3, up 11 days healthy, roles/pazny.ntfy/defaults/main.yml:11; grep-confirmed no default.config.yml shadow). ntfy v2.27.0 published 2026-08-04, roughly TWENTY-FOUR HOURS before this scan, and its security section is squarely on this batch's probe class. VERBATIM from the release notes: 'Limit message templates (Template: yes) to 32 KB, limit printf widths and precisions to below 1000, and limit indent/nindent to 100 spaces, preventing excessive memory use from a single small template.' This is the MEMORY half of a DoS whose CPU half nOS already carries: REM-132 leg (3) recorded v2.26.0's 'Prevent a CPU denial of service via message templates (Template: yes)', which added an execution TIMEOUT. A timeout bounds how LONG a template runs; it does not bound how much it ALLOCATES. A single small request body -- the amplification primitives are named in the fix itself: printf width/precision, and indent/nindent -- expands inside the template engine to an arbitrarily large string before any clock-based cap can fire. The pinned v2.26.3 therefore has the timeout and NOT the allocation cap. This matters more here than the raw severity suggests, for two reasons specific to nOS: the ntfy container is capped at mem_limit 512m (docker_mem_limit_light, the smallest tier in the estate, default.config.yml:347), so the allocation ceiling an attacker must reach to trigger an OOM-kill is the lowest of any service; and ntfy is the A9 notification-fanout transport, so OOM-killing it does not merely drop a service, it silently blinds the alerting path that would report the outage -- restart: unless-stopped brings it back but the in-flight notifications are gone. v2.27.0 also carries a second security item, verbatim: 'Exclude secrets from the config hash served to the web app, preventing a rather theoretical information leak' -- the vendor's own hedge is retained; no secret-bearing field is named. SOURCING CAVEAT, now confirmed for the third consecutive ntfy scan and worth restating because it is a permanent property of this component: binwiederhier/ntfy's GitHub security-advisories endpoint returns ZERO published advisories, OSV has no ntfy records, and NVD has no CVE for any of this. These are release-note-level fixes only -- do NOT cite a CVE, a GHSA, or a vendor CVSS for them. PROBE (resource_exhaustion_vectors) -- ntfy's own visitor rate limiting is the ONE limiter in the estate that is correctly wired, verified by reading the source rather than assuming: roles/pazny.ntfy/templates/server.yml.j2 sets behind-proxy: true and leaves proxy-forwarded-header at its X-Forwarded-For default, and ntfy v2.26.3 server/util.go extractIPAddressFromHeader documents and implements 'we first remove the trusted IP addresses from the list, and then take the RIGHT-MOST address in the list (as this is the one added by our proxy server)'. Traefik appends the real connecting client to the right of X-Forwarded-For, so the right-most entry is the genuine client and a caller who pre-poisons the header only prepends entries that are never read. The per-visitor buckets therefore hold: visitor-request-limit-burst 60 / replenish 5s, visitor-subscription-limit 30, visitor-attachment-total-size-limit 100M, visitor-attachment-daily-bandwidth-limit 500M, all at their defaults, plus the explicitly-set attachment-file-size-limit 15M and attachment-total-size-limit 5G. NOT SPOOFABLE -- recorded as verified-mitigated, not as a finding. ACTION: bump ntfy_version v2.26.3 -> v2.27.0 in roles/pazny.ntfy/defaults/main.yml:11. MITIGATED meanwhile: install_ntfy=false; the router ntfy@file carries authentik@file forward-auth (LIVE-CONFIRMED against the Traefik API), which gates the web UI, the admin surface AND the publish/API paths at ntfy.<tld>; auth-default-access deny-all + enable-signup false; container host-binds 127.0.0.1:2586 (LAN only when services_lan_access=true). Template rendering requires publish rights, so the exposure is insider-scoped, not anonymous.

Cycle-22 batch-43 ATTACK PROBE (2026-08-05, resource_exhaustion_vectors) -- THE PROBE'S FINDING OF RECORD, measured on this host, not theorised. CVE LEG IS CLEAN and that is the point: Home Assistant Core is CVE-clean at the pinned homeassistant_version 2026.6.0 (default.config.yml:1966 + roles/pazny.homeassistant/defaults/main.yml:10, in sync; live iiab-homeassistant-1 on homeassistant/home-assistant:2026.6.0, up 11 days healthy). The two advisories published since the 2026-07-23 look -- CVE-2026-66061 / GHSA-j23v-9672-677j and CVE-2026-66060 / GHSA-2xqv-hwrf-983f, both HIGH, both 2026-07-31, Companion app forwards NFC/QR tag scans to every configured server without user confirmation -- declare ecosystems 'ios' and 'android' with fix versions 2026.5.0 and 2026.5.3, i.e. they are COMPANION MOBILE APPS and N/A to the Core container, exactly like CVE-2026-54318 / CVE-2026-55844 / CVE-2026-44698 before them. No Core-server advisory has a fixed version newer than 2026.6.0. The exposure is CONFIGURATION. FOUR facts, each read from the running container: (1) THE ROUTER IS ANONYMOUS. Live GET http://127.0.0.1:8082/api/http/routers shows homeassistant@file, Host(`home.<tld>`), middlewares [security-headers@file, compress@file] -- NO authentik@file. traefik_auth_modes.homeassistant='oidc' means native OIDC, and native OIDC ADDS a Sign-in-with-Authentik button to HA's own login page; it does not put a wall in front of it. POST /auth/login_flow is reachable with no credentials. The 127.0.0.1:8123 host-bind constrains only the direct container port, not the Traefik path. (2) EVERY FAILED LOGIN COSTS A COST-12 BCRYPT. homeassistant/auth/providers/homeassistant.py validate_login hardcodes dummy = b'$2b$12$CiuFGszHx9eNHxPuQcwBWez4CwDTOcLTX5CbOpV6gef2nYuXkY7BO' and, when the username does not exist, executes bcrypt.checkpw(b'foo', dummy) with the comment 'check a hash to make timing the same as if user was found'. The anti-timing-attack defence is itself the amplifier: an UNKNOWN username is as expensive as a real one. MEASURED IN-CONTAINER ON THIS HOST: 207.7 ms per checkpw, averaged over five runs. The container is capped at cpus: 1.0 (docker_cpus_standard). 1000 ms / 207.7 ms = ~4.8 anonymous requests per second fully saturate Home Assistant's entire CPU allocation. Not a botnet -- one client, one thread, five requests a second. (3) THE BAN THAT WOULD STOP IT IS INERT. components/http/__init__.py sets ip_ban_enabled default=True but login_attempts_threshold default=NO_LOGIN_ATTEMPT_THRESHOLD = -1, and ban.py process_wrong_login returns early on `if KEY_BAN_MANAGER not in request.app or request.app[KEY_LOGIN_THRESHOLD] < 1: return` -- BEFORE the failed-attempt counter is incremented and before any ban is issued. So the enabled-looking ip_ban never fires for login flooding unless a positive threshold is explicitly configured. The live /config/configuration.yaml sets an http: block (use_x_forwarded_for + trusted_proxies) and sets NEITHER key. (4) SECOND, INDEPENDENT LEG -- REVERSE DNS. process_wrong_login runs `await hass.async_add_executor_job(gethostbyaddr, request.remote)` on every failed attempt, ahead of the threshold return, so each anonymous bad login also occupies a bounded executor thread for the duration of a blocking rDNS lookup. Against a source whose PTR resolution stalls, thread-pool occupancy is a cheaper exhaustion path than the CPU one. AMPLIFIED BY REM-169: there is no rateLimit and no inFlightReq middleware on this router, so nothing meters the request stream before it reaches any of the above. REACHABILITY, stated honestly and with the same caveat as REM-144: CONFIRMED anonymous from LAN/Tailscale (Traefik binds 0.0.0.0:443; the only precondition is host:443 plus the Host header). INTERNET reach is UNVERIFIED and NOT claimed -- split-horizon dnsmasq resolves the name to the host's own LAN address, so a local curl provably never leaves the LAN. Availability-only: no data is read, written, or disclosed. Rated HIGH on the same basis as REM-074 (calibre-web ReDoS, unauthenticated availability DoS) -- unauthenticated, single-client, trivially scripted, and it takes down the home-automation control plane. ACTION, in order: (a) set http.login_attempts_threshold to a positive integer (5 is the community-conventional value) in the ANSIBLE MANAGED http: block that roles/pazny.homeassistant already writes into /config/configuration.yaml, which activates the ip_ban_enabled=True that is already in force and makes leg (3) real; (b) attach a rateLimit middleware to homeassistant@file -- see REM-169, which is the estate-wide form of the same gap; (c) OPTIONAL and separate: consider traefik_auth_modes.homeassistant 'oidc' -> 'proxy' so Authentik fronts the login flow entirely, weighing it against the HA Companion apps and webhook/API integrations that would break behind forward-auth -- do NOT flip this without checking those consumers. NOTED, not filed: trusted_proxies includes 192.168.0.0/16, the whole LAN, which is broader than the 172.16.0.0/12 Docker range Traefik actually reaches from; it is unreachable today because the container host-binds 127.0.0.1:8123, so it is over-broad rather than exploitable -- tighten it when the file is next touched. HYGIENE, no security content: 2026.6.0 trails the current stable 2026.7.4 (2026-07-24) by one minor; no Core advisory sits between them, so this is a currency bump, not a fix.

items.remediation_detail: Cycle-22 batch-43 ATTACK PROBE (2026-08-05, resource_exhaustion_vectors) -- LIVE-CONFIRMED against the RENDERED config inside the running container, not the template. The edge applies NO request-rate limit and NO concurrent-connection cap to substantially every Tier-1 service. Evidence, in order of strength: `docker exec infra-traefik-1 grep -c 'rateLimit\|inFlightReq' /etc/traefik/conf.d/*.yml` returns middlewares.yml:0, services.yml:0, tls.yml:0 -- and services.yml is the 28016-byte file that carries every Tier-1 router. The source templates agree: roles/pazny.traefik/templates/dynamic/ contains middlewares.yml.j2, services.yml.j2 and tls.yml.j2, and a grep for rateLimit / inFlightReq / average / burst / amount across the whole directory returns nothing. WHAT MAKES THIS A FINDING RATHER THAN AN OMISSION: the same directory listing shows keap-ext.yml:1 and keap-ingest.yml:1 -- both DO carry rate limiting, and the live router dump confirms keap-ext@file bound to keap-ext-ratelimit@file and keap-ingest@file bound to keap-ingest-ratelimit@file. So the pattern is understood, implemented, wired and working in this codebase; it has simply been applied to exactly 2 of the ~30 file-provider routers, both belonging to one component (KEAP), while the other 28 got nothing. This is not 'rate limiting was never considered' -- it is a defence that exists and was never generalised. EXPOSURE: the live router dump shows the overwhelming majority of file-provider routers resolving with middlewares [security-headers@file, compress@file] and NO authentik@file -- among them authentik@file itself (public by design), onlyoffice@file (public by design, see REM-170), homeassistant@file (REM-168), plus gitea, gitlab, grafana, nextcloud, portainer, vaultwarden, wordpress, superset, open-webui, outline, jellyfin, n8n, node-red, miniflux, hedgedoc, bookstack, freescout, rustfs, woodpecker and offline-maps. Every one of those is an anonymously-reachable, completely unmetered path to a backend, over a 0.0.0.0:443 bind. Only firefly@file and ntfy@file, of this batch's five components, carry authentik@file -- and forward-auth is an authorization gate, not a rate limiter: the Authentik outpost round-trip itself is unmetered work an anonymous client can force. THIS IS THE MULTIPLIER FOR THE WHOLE BATCH. It is what converts REM-168 from 'HA hashes a password' into 'five anonymous requests per second take down the control plane', and it is what leaves onlyoffice -- the estate's heaviest CPU consumer, anonymous by design, capped at cpus 1.0 -- with no floor at all. Rated MEDIUM standing alone (availability-only, no confidentiality or integrity leg, and no evidence of exploitation) but it should be read together with REM-168 and REM-170 rather than in isolation. ACTION: add a shared rateLimit middleware to roles/pazny.traefik/templates/dynamic/middlewares.yml.j2 (Traefik's rateLimit is per-source-IP by default via its default sourceCriterion; keap-ext-ratelimit / keap-ingest-ratelimit are the in-repo precedent to copy the shape from) and append it to the middleware chain emitted for every router in services.yml.j2, with a per-service override var so heavy legitimate consumers -- nextcloud sync, jellyfin streaming, gitea/gitlab git-over-HTTPS, the onlyoffice document-conversion callbacks -- can be raised or exempted rather than broken. Consider inFlightReq alongside it for the slow-connection class; REM-076 (Traefik TCP Slowloris, resolved by version) closed the protocol-level variant of that, not the application-level one. Tune before enforcing: an under-set global limit on this estate breaks sync clients, and a broken sync client is a worse outcome than the DoS it prevents.

items.remediation_detail: Cycle-22 batch-43 CVE scan + ATTACK PROBE (2026-08-05, resource_exhaustion_vectors). THE PILOT HAS ACTIVATED AND THE STANDING CAVEAT CAME DUE. Every prior onlyoffice scan closed with the line 'the euro-office fork (ghcr.io/euro-office/documentserver, flipped via onlyoffice_image) tracks the same base -- verify ITS pinned base tag separately if that pilot activates', and then version-scanned the DECLARED pin. This batch checked the running container instead: `docker ps` shows b2b-onlyoffice-1 on ghcr.io/euro-office/documentserver:LATEST, up 11 days, healthy. The declared pin in roles/pazny.onlyoffice/defaults/main.yml:43-44 is onlyoffice/documentserver:9.3.1.2, and the commented euro-office block at lines 19-20 says in as many words 'onlyoffice_version: latest # ghcr has NO semver image tags yet'. So the live estate is running a floating tag. THREE CONSEQUENCES, in ascending order of seriousness. (1) The build is a PRERELEASE AND IT IS BEHIND THE DECLARED PIN: `docker exec b2b-onlyoffice-1 dpkg -l | grep documentserver` reports euro-office-documentserver 9.3.1-DEV.1 (arm64). 9.3.1-dev.1 is a dev cut of 9.3.1; the declared pin 9.3.1.2 is a later patch of the same minor. The service actually serving documents is therefore on an unreleased build BELOW the version every previous CLEAN verdict was issued against -- including the batch-32 and batch-24 findings that CVE-2026-41034 (XLS untrusted-pointer-dereference, info-leak / ASLR bypass) is cleared because 'fix <9.3.0, pin 9.3.1.2 is above it'. That specific conclusion survives (9.3.1-dev.1 is also above 9.3.0) but it survives by accident; the reasoning it rested on was about a version this host is not running. (2) IT CANNOT BE VERSION-SCANNED AT ALL. The image carries exactly one OCI label, org.opencontainers.image.version = '24.04' -- that is the Ubuntu base, not the DocumentServer version, and a scanner reading that label learns nothing about the application. There is no semver tag to query, ONLYOFFICE/DocumentServer's GitHub security-advisories endpoint returns ZERO published advisories, and no vendor advisory feed exists for the euro-office fork at all. Combined with 'latest', the running version is whatever ghcr served at pull time and can change under the estate on any recreate with no record. This component is currently OUTSIDE the scanner's reach, and 'CLEAN' for it has meant 'clean at a version we are not running'. (3) It is the estate's most attractive resource-exhaustion target, which is why it is filed on this probe rather than as pure supply-chain hygiene. traefik_auth_modes.onlyoffice='none' by design -- collaborative editing cannot sit behind forward-auth because the Nextcloud / Outline / BookStack integrations call it server-to-server -- and the live router dump confirms onlyoffice@file, Host(`office.<tld>`), middlewares [security-headers@file, compress@file, docserver-nocache@file], with no authentik@file and, per REM-169, no rateLimit. So the single heaviest CPU consumer in the estate (document conversion, rendering, font generation) sits anonymous and unmetered behind cpus: 1.0 / mem_limit 2g. The mitigation that holds and was re-verified: JWT_ENABLED=true with JWT_SECRET gates the document and conversion API, and USE_UNAUTHORIZED_STORAGE=false, so an anonymous caller reaches only /healthcheck (confirmed returning `true`) and the static welcome/web-apps assets (confirmed: GET /web-apps/apps/api/documents/api.js -> 200, 63253 bytes) -- static bytes, not conversion CPU. That JWT gate is the entire reason this is MEDIUM and not HIGH: without it, an anonymous unmetered conversion endpoint on a 1-CPU container would be the estate's cheapest full outage. ACTION: (a) pin the euro-office image to an immutable reference -- a digest (ghcr.io/euro-office/documentserver@sha256:5a1a8b7083856b309f09a5b06aa96f80182cbdfccddcae6c082ecf7a2b3cbf2b is the currently-resident build, created 2026-06-25T09:38:48Z) until the fork publishes semver tags, so the running version is at least RECORDED and reproducible; (b) record the upstream base the fork tracks (9.3.1-dev.1) in the role so future scans version-check the thing that is actually running, not the inert onlyoffice/documentserver pin; (c) revisit whether a -dev build belongs in the live path at all, or whether the pilot should track a released cut. Upstream context, unchanged and still true of the declared pin: latest upstream ONLYOFFICE CE remains 9.4.0 (2026-05-20), no DocumentServer CVE has published since the 2026-07-23 look, and the whole 12-month set is either fixed at/below 9.3.x (CVE-2026-41034, CVE-2025-68917/68935/68936, CVE-2025-5301) or belongs to a different ONLYOFFICE product (CVE-2025-6380 WordPress plugin, CVE-2026-41030 DesktopEditors, CVE-2026-38587 DocSpace, CVE-2026-33330 FileRise, CVE-2025-10254/10255 Projects/Community, CVE-2025-64766 NixOS packaging). install_onlyoffice=false by default; container host-binds 127.0.0.1:3015.

items.remediation_detail: Cycle-23 batch-44 CVE scan (2026-08-06, supply_chain_freshness). NEW, and it OVERTURNS the batch-32 disposition that v1.30.5 closes the mailpit tail. CVE-2026-67448 (GHSA-8r62-w5wh-fc5m), 'WebSocket origin check bypass via percent-encoded path', MODERATE CVSS 6.5, published 2026-07-28: affects >=1.29.0 <=1.30.5, FIXED 1.30.6. LIVE-CONFIRMED at the pin -- `docker ps` shows iiab-mailpit-1 running axllent/mailpit:v1.30.5, and the pin reads v1.30.5 at roles/pazny.mailpit/defaults/main.yml:21 (grep-confirmed NO default.config.yml shadow; default.config.yml:251 carries only mailpit_ui_port). MECHANISM: the WebSocket origin check reads the RAW request URI while Go's mux routes on the DECODED path, so a handshake to /%61pi/events reaches the /api/events handler having skipped the origin validation entirely. It is a REGRESSION of CVE-2026-22689 (GHSA-524m-q5m7-79mm, the original CSWSH item this queue closed at 1.28.2) -- the same class re-opened by a normalization mismatch rather than a new feature. THIS IS THE FIRST CONFIDENTIALITY LEG IN THE MAILPIT TAIL: REM-081..085, REM-112 and REM-131 were all availability-only (A:L, memory/CPU pressure); this one reads message data (sender, recipient, subject) cross-origin. WHY IT MATTERS MORE HERE THAN THE UPSTREAM 6.5 SUGGESTS, and equally why it is not rated HIGH -- both halves stated honestly. (a) The upstream advisory scopes the impact to 'default settings', and nOS IS that default: roles/pazny.mailpit/defaults/main.yml:31-32 set mailpit_ui_user and mailpit_ui_password to the empty string, the compose template gates MP_UI_AUTH behind `{% if mailpit_ui_user | length > 0 %}`, and `docker inspect iiab-mailpit-1` confirms NO MP_UI_AUTH in the live env -- the UI and REST API are unauthenticated. On the loopback path (127.0.0.1:8025) the origin check is therefore the ONLY control standing between a malicious page in any browser on the host and a live stream of every message the estate's mail sink captures; this CVE removes exactly that control. Mailpit is where Authentik invitations, password resets and the A18 invite-provisioning mail land, so the metadata is estate-wide. (b) Against that: the exposure is metadata (sender/recipient/subject), NOT message bodies or tokens; it needs an operator browser on the host to visit attacker content; and the EDGE route is gated -- roles/pazny.traefik/vars/main.yml:111 sets traefik_auth_modes.mailpit='proxy' (Authentik proxy outpost, admin tier), and a cross-site WS handshake to mail.<tld> will not carry a SameSite=Lax Authentik session cookie, so the edge leg is mitigated and the loopback leg is the real one. MEDIUM is the CVSS-consistent rating and matches the rest of the mailpit cluster. ACTION: bump mailpit_version v1.30.5 -> v1.30.6 in roles/pazny.mailpit/defaults/main.yml:21. Independently worth doing regardless of this CVE: set mailpit_ui_user/mailpit_ui_password so the loopback API is not anonymous. COVERED AT THE PIN, re-verified no action: GHSA-r553-m4fv-5v97 (fix 1.30.5), GHSA-w878-pj84-3j5v + GHSA-75mr-qw9x-3r39 (fix 1.30.4), CVE-2026-55187, CVE-2026-48824, CVE-2026-45713, CVE-2026-27808, CVE-2026-23829 -- REM-081..085 / REM-112 / REM-131 all stay resolved.

Cycle-23 batch-44 PROBE (2026-08-06, supply_chain_freshness -- FIRST RUN of this probe type). NOT a CVE. LIVE-CONFIRMED provenance gap: the ollama binary this estate runs does not come from where the playbook thinks it does. `brew info --json=v2 ollama` reports full_name 'pazny/local/ollama', tap 'pazny/local', installed 0.30.7_1 -- an OPERATOR-AUTHORED LOCAL TAP, not homebrew-core. `brew tap` confirms pazny/local is installed; `ollama --version` reports 0.30.7 and /opt/homebrew/bin/ollama is the binary the LaunchAgent execs (roles/pazny.openclaw/templates/com.ollama.agent.plist.j2:10). The playbook's only ollama install declaration is roles/pazny.openclaw/tasks/main.yml:9-13 -- `community.general.homebrew: name: ollama, state: latest` -- an UNQUALIFIED formula name, with no tap pin, no ollama_version variable anywhere in the repo (grep-confirmed: default.config.yml carries only ollama_max_loaded_models / _num_parallel / _keep_alive / _flash_attention tuning vars), and no post-install version assertion. THREE CONSEQUENCES, each verifiable. (1) The disposition this queue has leaned on for REM-096 -- recorded verbatim in 2026-04-08-vuln-report.md:651 as 'host brew state=latest floats past 0.17.1 (no ollama_version var to pin)' -- is TRUE TODAY ONLY BY ACCIDENT. It holds because the local tap happens to sit at 0.30.7, far past the 0.17.1 that fixed CVE-2026-7482; nothing in the repo checks it. Contrast frankenphp, which pins frankenphp_version and then runs `frankenphp --version` post-install and fails with an explicit diagnostic when the landed binary disagrees (default.config.yml:663-676 comment + pazny.wing/tasks/main.yml). Ollama, which terminates unauthenticated model-loading code paths, has no equivalent -- a floating install whose freshness claim is never measured is the 2026-08-01 'success markers must be written by a reader' shape applied to a version pin. (2) A blank on a fresh host has NO pazny/local tap, so `name: ollama` resolves to homebrew-core and installs a DIFFERENT BINARY. Per docs/archive/v07-overnight/v07-darwin27-homebrew-formula-tap-stability.md:21-23 and memory `ollama-brew-mlx-only-bottle`, core's bottle ships without llama-server, which makes every GGUF model return HTTP 500 -- so the reinstall-from-scratch guarantee that is nOS's central claim does not currently hold for the inference layer. That archive doc already names the tap 'an undocumented out-of-band hack'; this is the first time it has been filed as a security-queue item rather than a roadmap note. (3) The tap is unversioned, uncommitted and unreviewed: no formula in-repo, no checksum, no signature, no upgrade path the playbook can drive, and `state: latest` against an unqualified name can silently swing between the local tap and core depending on Homebrew's resolution order. RESIDUAL RISK is provenance and reproducibility, not a live exploit -- the mitigating control for the still-vendor-blocked REM-126 (CVE-2026-5757 GGUF quantization memory leak, no upstream fix) is unchanged and independent: com.ollama.agent.plist.j2 hard-sets OLLAMA_HOST=127.0.0.1:11434, so the API is loopback-only. ACTION (operator-supervised, not auto-fixable): (a) introduce an ollama_version var and assert the landed `ollama --version` against it, mirroring the frankenphp gate, so the REM-096 freshness claim is measured rather than assumed; (b) decide the tap question deliberately -- either vendor the HEAD formula into the repo as a committed, gated seam (option 3 in the archive doc) or add pazny/local to homebrew_taps and qualify the install name -- because today neither the tap nor its absence is expressed anywhere in the playbook.

items.remediation_detail: Cycle-23 batch-44 (2026-08-06, supply_chain_freshness). FRESHNESS ONLY -- the CVE leg is CLEAN and was re-verified from the authoritative sources, not inferred: GET /repos/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/security-advisories returns an EMPTY array (no GHSA has ever been published for this project) and an OSV query for crates.io/spacetimedb returns {}. No NVD or CISA hit in the 12-month window. What changed since batch-34 is only the distance to head: the pin v2.7.0-hotfix3 (2026-07-22) was upstream head at the last scan and is now TWO releases behind -- v2.7.1 (2026-07-30) and v2.8.0 (2026-08-05, i.e. the day before this scan). Both release bodies were read rather than assumed. NEITHER carries a security fix. v2.8.0 contains zero security-relevant lines. v2.7.1 is bug fixes (sequence-migration precheck, V10 column defaults, scheduled-reducer interval drift, a module-init task leak) and its ONE auth-adjacent entry is a REVERT, not a patch: 'The removal of the spacetimedb-jsonwebtoken and spacetimedb-jwks dependencies has been reverted due to Keats/jsonwebtoken#510. This restores the previous authentication behavior' (PR #5578). Keats/jsonwebtoken#510 was read directly and is a FUNCTIONAL/COMPATIBILITY bug, not a vulnerability -- the Header struct types extra fields as HashMap<String,String>, so RFC-7515-legal non-string header claims fail to deserialize; the proposed fix is to widen the type to serde_json::Value. It is worth recording only because SpacetimeDB's entire auth model is JWT/JWKS (roles/pazny.spacetimedb/defaults/main.yml header) and v2.7.1 therefore restores the dependency that path runs on. NO LIVE EXPOSURE: install_spacetimedb is false at default.config.yml:450, `docker ps` shows no spacetimedb container, and even when enabled the container host-maps to 127.0.0.1:<spacetimedb_port|3030> only, with traefik_auth_modes.spacetimedb='none' by design (a binary protocol cannot carry a forward-auth redirect). PIN HYGIENE re-verified GOOD: v2.7.0-hotfix3 is declared once, at default.config.yml:1652, with no role-defaults shadow (roles/pazny.spacetimedb/defaults/main.yml carries no version key) -- the 1bc5dcbb shadow deletion held here. ACTION: low-priority bump to v2.8.0 at the next supervised converge; nothing forces it.

Cycle-23 batch-44 PROBE (2026-08-06, supply_chain_freshness). THE PROBE'S STRUCTURAL FINDING OF RECORD, and it is filed LOW because it was MEASURED rather than asserted -- the measurement is what makes it worth keeping. tests/anatomy/test_image_pin_hygiene.py scans three surfaces: variable DECLARATIONS in default.config.yml, variable DECLARATIONS in roles/pazny.*/defaults/main.yml, and literal `image:` lines in templates/stacks/*/docker-compose.yml.j2. It does NOT scan roles/pazny.*/templates/compose.yml.j2 -- the per-role compose overrides that are the actual render path for every Tier-1 service. Twenty-eight image lines there carry a FLOATING Jinja fallback: `| default('latest')` in calibre_web, face, freepbx, gitea, gitlab, grafana, infisical, jellyfin, keap, kiwix, loki, mcp_gateway (mcp_grafana), metabase, n8n, offline_maps, outline, portainer, prometheus, qgis_server, rustfs, SPACETIMEDB, VAULTWARDEN, woodpecker (x2), wordpress; `| default('stable')` in homeassistant and nextcloud; `| default('main')` in open_webui. MAILPIT is a fourth variant -- roles/pazny.mailpit/templates/compose.yml.j2:26 falls back to `default('v1.20')`, a non-floating but ANCIENT tag that predates every mailpit CVE this queue has closed (REM-081..085, REM-112, REM-131, REM-171), so its fallback is arguably worse than 'latest' because it would silently pin to a known-vulnerable version and pass a floating-tag gate while doing it. MEASURED REACHABILITY: ZERO of the 28 are reachable today. Every one of those vars still has a live declaration (checked programmatically by parsing default.config.yml, default.credentials.yml and all 75 role defaults, then resolving each fallback's var against that set: 0 undeclared). The fallbacks are dead code as of this scan, which is precisely why this is LOW and not HIGH -- no floating tag is being rendered, and `docker ps` corroborates it for the live batch components (iiab-vaultwarden-1 on 1.37.0, iiab-mailpit-1 on v1.30.5, both exact pins, no 'latest'). WHY FILE IT ANYWAY: commit 1bc5dcbb 'refactor(pins): 38 version pins that could not win' deleted the shadowed duplicates, so there is now EXACTLY ONE declaration per pin. That was the right fix for the qgis miss (3d465e22) and it removed a real ambiguity -- but it also removed the redundancy that used to make these fallbacks unreachable by accident. Before, deleting one copy left the other and the tag stayed pinned; now a single deletion is the entire difference between a pinned tag and `latest`, and the gate CANNOT see that transition, because a deleted variable declares nothing left to scan. The gate would stay green through the exact edit that un-pins a service. This is the same shape the gate's own docstring already names -- 'scanning only one of two files is how a gate loses scope silently' -- one surface further out: the docstring fixed WHICH DECLARATIONS are read, and this finding is about the RENDER SITE that consumes them. ACTION: extend the gate with a fourth check over roles/pazny.*/templates/*.j2 asserting that every `image:` Jinja fallback is (a) non-floating AND (b) backed by a live declaration -- i.e. make the absence of a pin fail the gate, not silently satisfy it. The scan script used here is trivially portable into the test. Optionally drop the fallbacks entirely so an undefined pin raises rather than defaults; that is the stronger fix and is consistent with the 'a gate you can satisfy by editing the gate is not one' doctrine.
items.source: tests/anatomy/test_image_pin_hygiene.py + programmatic scan of roles/pazny.*/templates/*.j2 against all declared vars (this scan) + commits 1bc5dcbb, 3d465e22

items.remediation_detail: LIVE bone_secret committed to a PUBLIC repo and left in git history — CLOSED BY ROTATION, NOT BY REMOVAL, and this row records why. WHAT HAPPENED: building the face Anatomy/Pulse view on 2026-08-05, a real pulse_jobs row was copied out of the live database for use as a test fixture (files/anatomy/face/src/lib/anatomy/pulse.test.ts:29). Two of its three env values were replaced with obvious placeholders; the third, WING_EVENTS_HMAC_SECRET, was not. It was byte-identical to ~/.nos/secrets.yml's bone_secret and reached origin/dev on a PUBLIC GitHub repo at 13:03. DETECTED by the nightly gitleaks job at 03:01 the next morning — correctly, exit 1, one new finding, notification emitted. Fourteen hours of exposure. REMEDIATED 2026-08-06: (1) the fixture value replaced with a self-describing FAKE_ placeholder; (2) a pytest gate added (test_a_fixture_is_never_a_real_secret) that fails while the value is still in a working tree, because gitleaks cannot run before a commit exists; (3) an audit-chain KEY RING built (App\Model\AuditChain::chainKeys) so the secret became rotatable at all — it derives the tamper-evident chain key, so rotating it previously invalidated all 140,758 signed rows; (4) bone_secret ROTATED via `-e bone_secret_rotate=true`. Post-rotation verification, live: CHAIN-OK 145,789 rows with the ring; CHAIN-BROKEN at id=1 with the new key alone (the control that proves the ring is not merely permissive). The exposed value now signs nothing and only verifies the history it signed. WHY wontfix RATHER THAN A HISTORY REWRITE: the value remains in git history and on every clone and mirror. Removing it needs a force-push of a public branch, which breaks every clone, the Gitea mirror and Woodpecker's checkouts, and cannot un-publish what was already fetchable. Against that: the rotated-out key confers no capability. Bone binds 127.0.0.1:8099 and sits in traefik_skip_ids, so the endpoint it authenticates is unreachable off-host; forging audit rows with it additionally requires WRITE access to wing.db, and anyone holding that reads the CURRENT key out of ~/.nos/secrets.yml anyway. The rewrite would buy tidiness at the cost of every downstream checkout. WHAT WOULD REOPEN THIS: Bone binding anything other than loopback, or the audit-chain key ceasing to derive from bone_secret without the ring following it. The first is worth a gate; filed as follow-up rather than asserted here.
